purpose: Pre-registered bounded selection-window screen for the risk-aware ownership structure; not the dynamic four-reference acceptance gate.

protection_allocation.portfolio_cap: unchanged from the coarse core_fraction structure
protection_allocation.cross_section: retain holdings by descending close-time causal trend strength and reduce the weakest holdings first

recovery_invariants.ordinary_recovery_buy_materiality: shared with the execution engine's one-percent-of-NAV order floor

selection_objective: maximize the minimum candidate wealth divided by same-engine passive wealth
treat return preservation as the primary objective
only after return qualification, maximize the minimum passive drawdown minus candidate drawdown
then maximize the median passive drawdown minus candidate drawdown
then compare turnover, costs and stability
prefer the larger core fraction only as an exact deterministic tie-break

acceptance_relationship.formal_return_hard_gate: quant terminal wealth must reach the highest of the four references in every mandatory exact case
acceptance_relationship.formal_drawdown_role: secondary optimization objective after the return hard gate
acceptance_relationship.ideal_drawdown_target: strictly below the worst maximum drawdown among the four references in the same exact case

limitations: This screen cannot pass the dynamic relative contract because exact four-reference results are incomplete.
The passive baseline is a same-engine diagnostic, not a substitute for the four read-only reference strategies.
The 2026 final-evaluation window is not read or used to choose the structure.
A selected structure remains research-only until every mandatory exact case has complete references and meets the return hard gate.
Drawdown remains mandatory to measure and optimize even though its ideal target is not the economic hard gate.
Backtest results do not guarantee future returns.

selected_structure.basis: highest minimum return retention among the frozen 0.7/0.8/0.9 structures while improving drawdown in all seven selection cases
